Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Gradual p99 latency increase for hosted inference — investigation & next steps

Hi Jordan / Brightline team,

We wanted to make you aware of a gradual but measurable increase in p99 latency for hosted text-generation requests that started early this morning in our us-west region. Your workloads that frequently use long-context sequences (>= 4k tokens) have seen the largest impact; we estimate the p99 has shifted from ~320ms to ~870ms for those request profiles.

What we know so far:
- Trigger: a routing change rolled out at 03:40 PDT that broadened the set of hosts eligible for serving long-sequence requests.
- Symptom: increased KV cache miss rate and higher tail latencies for requests that normally benefited from warmed local caches.
- Scope: predominantly us-west hosted pool; only a subset of customers with long-context inference are affected.

Immediate actions were taking:
1) Rolling back the routing change for the affected pool (in progress). Expected completion within 45 minutes.
2) Running cache-warming jobs for hot prefixes to reduce cold-miss tail.
3) Increasing tracing + p99 alerting sensitivity for long-sequence paths and scheduling a post-incident RCA.

We will post continuous updates to our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-05-28-p99-drift (incident id: RDW-20270528-17). I'm copying our SRE and account leads; Marissa will follow up with an ETA for full mitigation and a draft postmortem once we have root cause confirmed.

Attachments: incident_snapshot_20270528.png (p99 graphs), query_sample_3542.log (sample slow requests)

Apologies for the disruption — we know tail latency matters for synchronous user flows.

— Avery

Avery / team — status update from SRE side:

1) Rollback completed at 09:50 PDT. The routing rule was reverted and affected instances have been drained & rebalanced. Early telemetry shows p99 for long-sequence requests trending back down toward baseline (~380ms) but with intermittent spikes while caches repopulate.
2) Cache warming: triggered targeted warmers for Brightline hot prefixes. Expect steady improvement over the next 60–90 minutes.
3) No automatic retries were introduced by our platform; we saw elevated client-side timeouts from customers who attempted aggressive retry policies. No requests were intentionally dropped by the gateway; some queued requests experienced extended queue times.

Planned follow-ups:
- Postmortem draft (internal) by EOD — I'll attach to the Drive folder: postmortem-BRG-3921.
- Proposal: implement a pre-warm step for new routing rules and a canary that exercises long-seq paths specifically.

Monica: can you confirm whether we should offer a one-week credit to Brightline as a gesture? We should coordinate with sales & finance.

Marissa
Director, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: root cause, mitigations, and next steps (Brightline — RDW-20270528-17)

Jordan — thanks again for the quick response and patience. Short summary and next steps; Ill paste this to the public incident page and share the internal RCA once finalized.

Root cause (confirmed):
- A routing configuration change broadened candidate hosts for long-sequence inference without warming KV caches on those hosts. The change increased inter-host KV misses by ~6x for long-context requests during initial traffic shift, producing the p99 deterioration.

Immediate mitigations taken (completed):
- Reverted the routing change (09:50 PDT).
- Targeted cache warmers for Brightline hot prefixes (09:55 PDT onwards).
- Increased p99 and cache-miss telemetry granularity and alerting.

Short-term product actions (next 7 days):
- Implement an explicit cache-warm step in routing-rollout playbooks; require canary traffic that includes long-sequence patterns before full rollout.
- Add automatic fallback to the previous routing set when p99 rises above a safety threshold.
- Create a warm-cache simulator to predict tail impact for routing changes.

Customer offer and compensation:
- Redwood will apply a service credit equivalent to one week of hosted inference fees for Brightline's primary account (BRG-3921); Monica will coordinate the credit process with Finance and follow up by Monday.

Work items / ownership:
- Marissa: finalize RCA doc and post to Drive by EOD (postmortem-draft-avery-v1.docx).
- Grace: instrumenting new warm-cache rollout guard rails (ownership: infra; ETA 2027-06-04).
- Monica: confirm credit and communication with Brightline commercial contact (ETA 2027-05-31).

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-05-28-p99-drift
Internal RCA draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C4/postmortem-BRG-3921
